CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with left-sided lower back pain. He has a significant surgical history of microdiscectomy performed in November 2020 for a ruptured disk that had wrapped around the spinal thecal sac. Initially post-operatively, he experienced severe nerve pain radiating down the leg and back and was treated with high-dose gabapentin, which was difficult to discontinue. Currently, he reports left-sided lower back pain that varies in location day to day but is generally localized to the area of prior surgery. Pain is exacerbated by bending over and occurs somewhat randomly. Pain improves with stretching. He has been taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily without complete relief. He has not tried icing. Denies current pain with forward flexion or extension. Reports pain with weightbearing while standing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed and patient denies other current health concerns.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Microdiscectomy November 2020

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has a significant other who encourages stretching and assists with pain management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Flexion: No pain with forward flexion at this time
Extension: No pain with extension
Weightbearing: Pain present while standing
Palpation: Pain with palpation to left L5 region; no pain with right-sided palpation
Motor: Dorsiflexion normal and intact bilaterally
Range of motion: Normal
No pain radiating down legs

RESULTS
X-ray of lumbar spine: No acute fractures or spinal bone abnormalities. Prior surgical site demonstrates appropriate healing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left-sided lower back pain, likely secondary to muscle strain from spinal misalignment
2. Discontinue ibuprofen; start meloxicam for pain management
3. Prescribed physical therapy through VA
4. Referral to pain management for evaluation and discussion of non-narcotic pain management strategies
5. Prescribed demerol for pain management
